steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: In January 1923, French and Belgian troops occupied the Ruhr, Germany's industrial heartland, after Germany defaulted on reparations payments. The German government responded with a policy of passive resistance. | Key Fact: By November 1923, the German mark had become virtually worthless. At the peak of hyperinflation, 4.2 trillion marks equalled $1 USD. A loaf of bread that cost 1 mark in 1919 cost 200,000 million marks by November 1923. Workers were paid twice daily and given time off to spend their wages before they lost further value. | Key Fact: The mark had been losing value since the war - Germany had funded WWI by printing money rather than raising taxes, doubling the money supply between 1914-1918. The Ruhr crisis accelerated an existing problem into a catastrophe. | Key
